title: Cars & Coffee at Pérez Art Museum This Saturday: Here's What to Expect
excerpt: PAMM's monthly Cars & Coffee is back this weekend with an expected 150+ vehicles lining the waterfront. From air-cooled Porsches to brand-new Revueltos, here's your guide to one of Miami's best morning car meets.
content:
If you haven't been to Cars & Coffee at the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM), you're missing one of the best-kept secrets in Miami's car scene. Every first Saturday of the month, the museum's waterfront parking area transforms into a curated open-air car show with Biscayne Bay as the backdrop.

What to Expect

Last month's event drew over 150 vehicles, and this Saturday is expected to be even bigger. The usual suspects — a rotating cast of 911s, a handful of Ferraris, and enough G-Wagons to invade a small country — will be joined by some special appearances. Word on the street is that a local collector is bringing his newly delivered Lamborghini Revuelto, one of the first in South Florida.

The Vibe

Unlike some of Miami's flashier meets, PAMM Cars & Coffee has a more curated, relaxed atmosphere. Think less rev-battle and more genuine conversation between enthusiasts. You'll find everyone from 20-year-old JDM fanatics to 70-year-old Ferrari collectors, and that's exactly what makes it special.

Practical Info

Time: 8 AM – 11 AM (show up by 7:30 if you want to display your car)

Location: Pérez Art Museum Miami, 1103 Biscayne Blvd

Parking: The museum garage opens at 7 AM. Street parking along Biscayne is free before 9 AM on weekends.

Tips: Bring sunscreen (there's minimal shade), grab a coffee from the museum café, and don't forget your camera. The lighting off the bay in the morning is photographer's paradise.

After the Meet

Most attendees roll out to Wynwood for brunch after. Kyu, Salty Donut, and Zak the Baker are all within a 10-minute cruise. It's become an unofficial tradition — cars, coffee, then carbs.

See you Saturday. 🏎️

title: Account Spotlight: @rfrsh.miami — South Florida's Cleanest Car Builds
excerpt: From widebody GT3s to slammed NSXes, this Miami-based Instagram account curates the best modified car content in South Florida. Here's why you should be following them.
content:
In a sea of Miami car content accounts, @rfrsh.miami stands out for one simple reason: taste. While other accounts chase clout with burnout videos and rev battles, RFRSH focuses on what actually matters — the builds.

What They Do

Run by a group of local car enthusiasts, @rfrsh.miami documents South Florida's best modified and exotic cars through clean photography and detailed build features. Their feed is a masterclass in automotive photography — dramatic lighting, interesting angles, and a consistent aesthetic that makes scrolling through their grid genuinely enjoyable.

Recent Highlights

The Bayside Blue R34 GT-R: They recently featured a legally imported Nissan Skyline R34 GT-R that showed up at the Wynwood meet. The photos captured every detail of the car's N1 motor and original interior. This is the kind of car content that makes you stop scrolling.

Widebody 992 GT3 on Brixton Forged: A local owner's Guards Red GT3 with a full Manthey Racing kit and custom Brixton Forged wheels. The shoot was done at sunrise on Key Biscayne — stunning backdrop for a stunning car.

1973 Porsche 911 Carrera RS Tribute: A backdated 911 build done by a Hialeah shop, shot in front of the Marine Stadium. Old school meets old school.

Liberty Walk NSX: A first-gen Acura NSX with the full Liberty Walk widebody treatment, sitting on air suspension in the Design District. Controversial? Maybe. Photogenic? Absolutely.

Why Follow

If you care about car culture — not just car flexing — this is the account to follow. They also host occasional meetups and photo shoots, so it's a great way to connect with the local scene.

Give them a follow: @rfrsh.miami on Instagram

title: Just Landed at RMC Miami: A 2024 McLaren 750S Spider in Volcano Yellow
excerpt: One of Miami's top exotic dealers just took delivery of a head-turning McLaren 750S Spider in the rare Volcano Yellow spec. We've got the details on this $380K open-top supercar.
content:
If you've driven past RMC Miami on NW 36th Street recently, you might have noticed something blindingly yellow in their showroom. That would be the brand-new 2024 McLaren 750S Spider that just landed — and it's a spec that'll stop traffic even by Miami standards.

The Spec

Exterior: Volcano Yellow — one of McLaren's most vibrant MSO colors. It's the kind of paint that photographs itself.

Interior: Carbon Black Alcantara with yellow contrast stitching and a carbon fiber steering wheel. The electrochromic roof panel goes from transparent to opaque at the push of a button.

Performance: The 750S packs McLaren's 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8, now producing 740 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. 0-60 in 2.7 seconds. Top speed: 206 mph with the roof down. It's not just fast — it's McLaren's most powerful series-production convertible ever.

Why This Spec Matters

Volcano Yellow is rarely ordered in Miami, where most buyers gravitate toward silvers, whites, and blacks. This makes it a standout spec — both for driving and as a collector piece. The 750S replaced the 720S and brought significant improvements in aero, chassis dynamics, and that glorious engine tune.

About RMC Miami

RMC (formerly known as Riva Motorsports & Marine) has quietly become one of South Florida's most trusted exotic dealers. Their inventory regularly includes McLarens, Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and Bentleys, with a reputation for transparency and well-documented vehicle histories.

Price: Listed at approximately $380,000. Contact RMC Miami for details.

If yellow isn't your thing, they've also got a Silica White 750S Coupe and a McLaren Artura in Flux Green on the floor. Worth a visit.

title: The Cars of Miami Vice: A Complete Guide to Every Iconic Ride
excerpt: From the fake Daytona Spyder to the real Testarossa, Miami Vice didn't just define 1980s television — it transformed Miami's relationship with exotic cars forever. Here's the complete automotive history of the show.
content:
The Car That Started It All: The "Daytona"

When Miami Vice premiered in September 1984, Sonny Crockett wasn't driving a Ferrari at all. His black sports car was actually a 1972 De Tomaso Mangusta-based replica of a Ferrari 365 GTS/4 Daytona Spyder, built by McBurnie Coachcraft in California. It looked the part on screen, but Ferrari was not amused.

Enzo Ferrari himself reportedly hated that a fake Ferrari was the star of America's hottest show. So Ferrari did something unprecedented: they gave the production two brand-new Testarossas. For free. The only condition? Destroy the replica.

The White Testarossa

In the Season 3 premiere ("When Irish Eyes Are Crying," 1986), the fake Daytona was spectacularly blown up, and Crockett rolled into the next scene in a gleaming white 1986 Ferrari Testarossa. Television history was made.

The white Testarossa became arguably the most famous car in TV history. Its side strakes, pop-up headlights, and flat-12 soundtrack became synonymous with 1980s Miami. Ferrari reportedly saw a 40% increase in US sales the year after the Testarossa appeared on the show.

Two Testarossas were used during filming — one hero car for close-ups and one stunt car. After the show ended in 1989, the hero car was donated to a museum. It sold at Barrett-Jackson in 2015 for $1.95 million.

Tubbs' Cadillac

Ricardo Tubbs (Philip Michael Thomas) drove a 1964 Cadillac Coupe DeVille convertible in black. While not as flashy as Crockett's rides, it was perfectly suited to the character — smooth, understated, and effortlessly cool.

The Villain Cars

Miami Vice was equally famous for its villain vehicles. Drug lords rolled in black Lamborghini Countachs, white Rolls-Royce Corniche convertibles, and the occasional Porsche 928. The show established the visual language that Miami still speaks: exotic cars equal power.

The Legacy

Before Miami Vice, South Florida wasn't particularly known for its car culture. After Miami Vice, it became the exotic car capital of America. Dealers like Prestige Imports and Braman saw a boom in exotic sales. The show essentially created the market that places like RMC Miami, Curated, and South Beach Exotic Rentals now serve.

Today, you can still spot white Testarossas cruising Ocean Drive — a living tribute to the show that made Miami and exotic cars inseparable. 🌴

title: Why Pre-2000 Porsche 911s Are Exploding in Value in Miami
excerpt: Air-cooled 911s have gone from $30K driver's cars to six-figure collectibles in under a decade. Miami is ground zero for this market — here's why, and what you should buy before prices climb higher.
content:
If you've been eyeing an air-cooled Porsche 911, the bad news is you're already late. The good news? There might still be time — if you know where to look and what to buy.

The Numbers

Let's talk data. A clean 1989 Porsche 911 Carrera (964 generation) that sold for $35,000 in Miami in 2016 is now worth $85,000-$120,000 depending on spec and condition. A 1995 993 Carrera that was a $45,000 car five years ago now commands $90,000-$150,000. 993 Turbo S? You're looking at $350,000+ for a good one.

The air-cooled 911 market has appreciated roughly 15-20% annually in South Florida over the past five years — outperforming the S&P 500, real estate, and most alternative investments.

Why Miami?

Several factors make Miami the epicenter of this market:

Climate: No salt, no snow, no rust. Florida cars survive decades without the corrosion that kills northeastern examples. A "Florida car" commands a 10-15% premium nationally.

Demographics: Miami's influx of wealth from tech, crypto, finance, and Latin American money has created a deep pool of buyers who want tangible, enjoyable assets.

Community: Miami has one of the most active air-cooled Porsche communities in the US. Shops like Finsport and Lüfteknic (not far in Atlanta) keep these cars running perfectly.

What to Buy Now

Best value: 1985-1989 Carrera 3.2 (G-body). Still findable under $80K in Miami. The last of the "affordable" air-cooleds.

Best investment: 1995-1998 993 Carrera S or 4S. The last air-cooled 911, wide body, increasingly rare. $120-180K now, likely $200K+ within 3 years.

Dream buy: 1973 Carrera RS 2.7. If you can find one under $1M, buy it immediately.

Where to Shop

In South Florida, check Suncoast Parts (they know every air-cooled 911 for sale within 100 miles), Bring a Trailer for transparent auction pricing, and the PCA Gold Coast Region classifieds. Avoid sight-unseen purchases — always get a PPI from a Porsche specialist.

title: Inside Curated: Miami's Most Exclusive Exotic Car Gallery
excerpt: Part dealer, part art gallery, part private club — Curated in Miami is redefining how the ultra-wealthy buy exotic cars. We got a look inside their invite-only showroom.
content:
You won't find Curated on any car dealer map. There's no flashing signage, no balloon arch, no "SALE" banners. From the outside, their Miami location looks more like a contemporary art gallery. That's entirely by design.

The Concept

Founded by a group of collectors who were tired of the traditional dealer experience, Curated operates more like a private members' club than a car dealership. Their inventory reads like a car enthusiast's fantasy: Pagani Huayras, Ferrari Monzas, McLaren Sennas, and the occasional hypercar that hasn't even been publicly announced yet.

The showroom itself is museum-quality. Cars are displayed on raised platforms with gallery-style lighting. Each vehicle comes with a digital provenance package — full ownership history, service records, and a condition report that would satisfy Christie's auction house.

What Sets Them Apart

Curation over volume: While traditional exotic dealers might stock 50-100 cars, Curated typically has 15-20 at any time. Every car is hand-selected, inspected, and detailed to concours standards before it hits the floor.

Privacy: Transactions are discreet. Many of their clients are high-profile individuals who don't want their purchases splashed across social media. Curated offers private viewing appointments and white-glove delivery anywhere in the world.

Community: They host exclusive events for clients — private track days at Homestead, invite-only dinners, and preview events for incoming inventory. It's as much a social club as a business.

Current Highlights

At the time of writing, their collection reportedly includes a Porsche 918 Spyder with under 500 miles, a Ferrari LaFerrari in Bianco Avus, and one of the few Bugatti Chiron Pur Sports delivered to the US. Total showroom value? Conservatively north of $15 million.

Visit them at curatedcollection.com

title: Supercar Saturdays Bal Harbour: The Ultimate Guide for First-Timers
excerpt: Thinking about checking out Supercar Saturdays at Bal Harbour? Here's everything you need to know — when to arrive, where to park, what to expect, and the unwritten rules of Miami's biggest weekly car meet.
content:
Supercar Saturdays at Bal Harbour Shops is the gold standard of Miami's weekly car meet scene. Every Saturday morning, hundreds of car enthusiasts descend on the luxury shopping center's parking area to show off, admire, and talk cars. Here's your first-timer's guide.

The Basics

When: Every Saturday, roughly 8 AM to 11 AM. The real action starts around 8:30.

Where: Bal Harbour Shops, 9700 Collins Ave, Bal Harbour FL 33154. The car meet happens in the main parking lot.

Cost: Free to attend, free to display your car.

When to Arrive

If you want to display your car: Arrive by 7:30 AM. The best spots go fast, and the organizers (informally) direct traffic to group similar cars together. Exotics tend to cluster near the main entrance.

If you're just spectating: 9 AM is the sweet spot. All the cars are in place, the crowd is buzzing, and you've got a solid hour before things start wrapping up.

What to Expect

On any given Saturday, you'll see 100-200+ vehicles. The typical mix includes:

Exotics: Ferraris, Lamborghinis, McLarens, and the occasional Pagani or Koenigsegg. Miami has one of the highest concentrations of exotic cars per capita in the US.

Classics: Vintage Porsches, muscle cars, and restored American classics. The classic contingent is smaller but always impressive.

Modified: Built Supras, GT-Rs, widebody BMWs, and the South Florida JDM scene in full force.

Luxury: Rolls-Royces, Bentleys, and enough Mercedes-AMGs to fill a dealership.

Unwritten Rules

🚫 Don't touch the cars. Seriously. Don't lean on them, don't open doors, don't sit in them unless invited.

📸 Ask before photographing people (cars are fair game).

🔇 No revving battles. The organizers and Bal Harbour security will shut it down fast.

🤝 Talk to people. The whole point is community. Most owners love talking about their cars.

See you next Saturday. 🏎️

title: The 5 Best Exotic Cars Under $150K You Can Buy in Miami Right Now
excerpt: You don't need half a million dollars to own an exotic in Miami. These five cars deliver supercar thrills at (relatively) attainable prices — and they're all available in South Florida right now.
content:
The dream of exotic car ownership is more attainable than you think — especially in Miami, where the sheer volume of luxury vehicles means depreciation works in the buyer's favor. Here are five genuinely exotic cars you can buy in South Florida for under $150K.

1. Porsche 911 Turbo (997.2) — $85,000-$130,000

The 997.2 Turbo might be the greatest all-around sports car ever built. Twin-turbo flat-six making 500 hp, PDK or manual transmission, all-wheel drive that handles Miami's summer downpours, and Porsche reliability. They've bottomed out in depreciation and are starting to climb. Buy now.

Look for: Sport Chrono, PCCB brakes, manual transmission (premium of $15-20K over PDK).

2. Audi R8 V10 (Gen 1) — $75,000-$120,000

The original R8 with the screaming 5.2L V10 is a genuine supercar that you can daily drive without drama. The naturally aspirated V10 revs to 8,700 RPM and sounds like a junior Lamborghini (because it basically is — same engine family as the Gallardo/Huracán).

Look for: V10 Plus models, manual gated shifter (increasingly rare and valuable), carbon ceramic brakes.

3. Ferrari California T — $100,000-$140,000

The California T is Ferrari's most approachable modern model — a twin-turbo V8 grand tourer with a retractable hardtop. Is it the most hardcore Ferrari? No. Is it a gorgeous, comfortable, genuinely fun Ferrari you can drive every day in Miami? Absolutely.

Look for: Handling Speciale package, Daytona-style seats, bright colors (they look best in Rosso Corsa or Blu Pozzi).

4. Lamborghini Gallardo LP560-4 — $90,000-$135,000

The Gallardo is still one of the most visually dramatic cars on the road. The LP560-4 is the sweet spot of the range — 560 hp V10, e-gear or manual, and that unmistakable Lamborghini presence. In Miami, a Gallardo gets nearly as much attention as a Huracán at half the price.

Look for: LP560-4 Spyder for the full Miami experience. Manual cars command a premium but are worth it.

5. Aston Martin DB11 V8 — $110,000-$145,000

The DB11 is the car James Bond would drive if he lived in Brickell. Mercedes-AMG twin-turbo V8, stunning British design, and a grand touring experience that nothing else in this price range can match. Early V8 models have depreciated into our range and they're absolute bargains.

Look for: V8 over V12 (more reliable, better balanced), Launch Edition, any color that isn't silver.

title: Prestige Imports Lamborghini Miami Takes Delivery of the Revuelto — Here's What It Costs
excerpt: South Florida's authorized Lamborghini dealer has received its first allocation of the Revuelto, Lamborghini's 1,001-hp hybrid V12 supercar. The price? Starting at $608,358 — before options.
content:
Prestige Imports on Collins Avenue in North Miami Beach has been the go-to Lamborghini dealer in South Florida for decades. This week, they received their first batch of the most important Lamborghini in a generation: the Revuelto.

The Car

The Revuelto is Lamborghini's first series-production hybrid — and it's a monster. A naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 paired with three electric motors produces a combined 1,001 horsepower. Zero to 60 in 2.5 seconds. Top speed: 217 mph. It's the most powerful Lamborghini ever built.

But the headline number doesn't tell the whole story. The Revuelto can drive up to 6 miles on pure electric power — enough to silently cruise through South Beach at 3 AM without waking the neighbors. It's a hypercar that can also be a gentleman.

The Price

Base MSRP starts at $608,358 before destination. But this is Lamborghini — nobody orders a base Revuelto. Add the Ad Personam interior customization ($15-30K), carbon fiber exterior package ($12K), Stile Edition paint ($8K), and the typical Miami buyer's options list, and you're looking at $680,000-$750,000 as delivered.

The Wait

Here's the reality: if you haven't already placed an order, you're looking at a 2+ year wait. Prestige Imports reportedly has a waitlist that extends into 2028. Allocation priority goes to existing Lamborghini owners and VIP clients — as it always does with flagship models.

For those who can't wait, expect the secondary market to command a $100-200K premium over sticker for the first year of deliveries. Several Miami-area Revueltos have already been pre-sold on the secondary market for north of $800K.

See It In Person

Prestige Imports typically displays new flagship arrivals in their main showroom for the first week. If you want to see the Revuelto up close, stop by their showroom at 14800 Biscayne Blvd, North Miami Beach. No appointment needed — just walk in.

More info: prestigeimports.net

title: Spotted in Miami: The Best Exotic Car Sightings This Week
excerpt: From a Bugatti Chiron on Brickell to a convoy of Rolls-Royces in South Beach, it was another wild week for car spotting in Miami. Here are the highlights from @exoticspottermiami.
content:
Every week, Miami delivers automotive eye candy that most cities only see at car shows. Thanks to the eagle-eyed community of local car spotters — especially @exoticspottermiami — we're rounding up the best sightings from the past seven days.

🏆 Sighting of the Week: Bugatti Chiron Sport in Brickell

Spotted Tuesday afternoon on Brickell Avenue near Cipriani, a Bugatti Chiron Sport in Atlantic Blue over French Racing Blue. This is one of approximately 12 Chirons registered in Miami-Dade County. The owner was heading to lunch — casually driving a $3.3 million car to get pasta. Only in Miami.

Rolls-Royce Convoy on Ocean Drive

Saturday night on Ocean Drive brought a convoy of five — yes, five — Rolls-Royces rolling in formation: two Cullinans (one matte black, one white), a Dawn convertible in Salamanca Blue, a Ghost in Arctic White, and bringing up the rear, a Phantom Extended in Bohemian Red. Total fleet value: approximately $2.5 million.

Ferrari SF90 XX Stradale at Bal Harbour

One of Ferrari's most extreme road cars was spotted at the Bal Harbour Shops valet on Thursday. The SF90 XX Stradale, with its 1,016 horsepower and fixed rear wing, is limited to 799 units worldwide. This one wore Rosso Corsa with racing stripes — the classic spec. Estimated value: $850,000+.

Pagani Huayra Roadster on I-95

Perhaps the most surprising sighting: a Pagani Huayra Roadster BC was photographed merging onto I-95 South near the Golden Glades interchange on Wednesday morning. Spec: exposed carbon fiber with blue accents. Only 40 Roadster BCs were made, at approximately $3.5 million each. Where was it heading? Unknown. But wherever it was going, it was getting there in style.

Honorable Mentions

• Matte green Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato on the MacArthur Causeway
• Toyota 2000GT (!!!) at Supercar Saturday — worth over $1 million
• A pristine DeLorean DMC-12 in Wynwood, complete with a flux capacitor prop

Got a sighting? Follow and tag @exoticspottermiami on Instagram.

title: Lamborghini Urus for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Dealers & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: Looking for a Lamborghini Urus for sale in Miami? Here's your complete 2026 guide to pricing, the best dealers, model comparisons, and what to know before buying South Florida's most popular super SUV.
content:
The Lamborghini Urus has become the unofficial SUV of Miami. Drive down Collins Avenue, cruise through Brickell, or park at Bal Harbour Shops, and you'll spot one every few minutes. If you're searching for a Lamborghini Urus for sale in Miami, you're not alone — it's the most sought-after luxury SUV in South Florida, and the market in 2026 has some interesting dynamics.

Lamborghini Urus for Sale in Miami: Current Market Overview

The Urus lineup has expanded significantly since its 2018 debut. In 2026, Miami buyers have three main options on dealer lots:

ModelHorsepower0-60 MPHApprox. Price (Miami)Availability
Urus S657 HP3.5 sec$235,000 – $270,000Good — regular allocations
Urus Performante657 HP3.3 sec$275,000 – $320,000Moderate — higher demand
Urus SE (PHEV)789 HP3.4 sec$320,000 – $380,000Limited — new for 2025+

Pre-owned Urus models from 2019–2023 are also plentiful in Miami, typically ranging from $165,000 to $220,000 depending on mileage and spec. The market has softened from the pandemic-era premiums, which is great news for buyers.

Where to Buy a Lamborghini Urus in Miami

Miami has more Lamborghini inventory than almost any city in the U.S. Here are the top dealers for Lamborghini Urus for sale in the area:

Prestige Imports — The Authorized Dealer

Located at 14700 S Dixie Hwy in North Miami Beach, Prestige Imports is Miami's official Lamborghini dealer and one of the highest-volume Lamborghini retailers in the country. They get priority allocations for new models like the Urus SE and typically have 15–25 Urus models (new and CPO) in stock at any time.

Why buy here: Factory warranty, Lamborghini Certified Pre-Owned program, and first access to limited editions.

Curated — The Boutique Option

In Wynwood, Curated operates as a gallery-style exotic dealership. They specialize in low-mileage, well-spec'd Urus models — think custom Mansory builds, Ad Personam colors, and rare configurations you won't find at the franchise dealer.

RMC Miami & Independent Dealers

For competitive pricing on pre-owned Urus models, independent dealers like RMC Miami (NW 36th Street), Exotic Car Trader, and iLusso often undercut franchise pricing by 5–10%. Just make sure to get a pre-purchase inspection (PPI) from an independent Lamborghini specialist.

Lamborghini Urus Pricing in Miami vs. National Average

Miami typically commands a slight premium on Urus pricing — usually 3–5% above national averages — because of relentless local demand. However, the flip side is that Miami has more inventory to choose from, which gives you better negotiating leverage on spec and color.

Pro tip: If you're flexible on color, you can save $10,000–$15,000 by choosing a Urus that's been sitting on a lot for 60+ days. White and black move fastest in Miami; bolder colors like Verde Mantis or Blu Astraeus tend to sit longer.

What to Know Before Buying a Urus in Miami

Insurance Costs

In Miami-Dade County, expect to pay $4,500–$8,000 per year for full coverage on a Urus, depending on your driving record and coverage limits. South Florida's insurance rates are among the highest in the country for luxury vehicles. Shop around — companies like Hagerty and Chubb often beat standard carriers for high-value SUVs.

Maintenance

The Urus shares its platform with the Audi RS Q8 and Bentley Bentayga, which means parts are more accessible than you'd expect for a Lamborghini. Annual maintenance runs $2,000–$4,000 for routine service. The big-ticket item is brakes: a full carbon-ceramic brake replacement runs $15,000–$20,000, typically needed every 30,000–40,000 miles.

Miami-Specific Considerations

  • Salt air: Miami's coastal environment can accelerate corrosion on brake components. Consider ceramic coating for the calipers and undercarriage protection.
  • Speed bumps: The Urus handles Miami's aggressive speed bumps better than any Lamborghini before it, but the Performante's stiffer suspension can be harsh on rough Brickell roads.
  • Parking: At 201 inches long, the Urus fits in most standard parking spots — unlike trying to squeeze a Huracán into a Publix parking lot.

Urus S vs. Urus Performante vs. Urus SE: Which One for Miami?

For most Miami buyers, the Urus S is the sweet spot. It's the most comfortable daily driver, has the best ride quality for Miami's pockmarked roads, and the price difference versus the Performante lets you spend more on the options that actually matter — like the Bang & Olufsen sound system, the Akrapovič exhaust, or a full Ad Personam interior.

The Performante is for the buyer who wants the sharpest driving dynamics and doesn't mind a stiffer ride. The fixed rear spoiler and matte black accents give it a more aggressive look that plays well in Miami.

The Urus SE is the most powerful and the most future-proof, with its plug-in hybrid drivetrain offering about 37 miles of electric range. It's the one to get if you want bragging rights on horsepower (789 HP) and prefer silent cruising around South Beach at night.

Bottom Line

If you're shopping for a Lamborghini Urus for sale in Miami, 2026 is actually a good time to buy. Inventory is healthy, premiums have normalized, and the model range has never been better. Start at Prestige Imports for new models or browse Curated and RMC Miami for pre-owned gems. And if you want our take on the best value in the segment right now — a well-spec'd 2023 Urus S with under 10,000 miles is the play.

title: Ferrari Lease Deals in Miami: What to Expect in 2026
excerpt: Thinking about leasing a Ferrari in Miami? Here's what Ferrari lease deals actually look like in 2026 — monthly payments, residuals, dealer tips, and why Miami is one of the best cities to lease an exotic.
content:
Leasing a Ferrari sounds like a fantasy, but in Miami it's surprisingly common. Between the city's car-obsessed culture and Florida's tax advantages, a Ferrari lease is how many South Florida drivers get behind the wheel of Maranello's finest without committing to a $300K+ purchase. If you're exploring Ferrari lease deals in Miami, here's what the market actually looks like in 2026.

Ferrari Lease Deals: How They Work in 2026

Ferrari Financial Services (FFS) handles leasing directly through authorized dealers. Unlike mainstream brands where you negotiate a money factor and residual, Ferrari leases are structured more like luxury financing — and the terms are better than you might expect.

ModelMSRP RangeTypical Lease (36 mo.)Down PaymentResidual Value
Roma$245,000 – $280,000$2,800 – $3,400/mo$25,000 – $40,00055–60%
296 GTB$330,000 – $380,000$3,800 – $4,500/mo$35,000 – $50,00052–58%
SF90 Stradale$550,000 – $650,000$6,500 – $8,000/mo$60,000 – $80,00050–55%
F80 (new)$3,600,000+Not typically leased——

These numbers assume strong credit (720+), first-time Ferrari buyer status, and Miami-area dealer pricing. Existing Ferrari owners — especially those with purchase history at their dealer — often negotiate better money factors.

Why Miami Is Ideal for a Ferrari Lease

Florida is one of the best states in the country for leasing any luxury vehicle, and Ferrari leases in particular benefit from several Miami-specific advantages:

  • No state income tax: More of your income goes toward that monthly payment.
  • Sales tax on payments only: In Florida, you pay sales tax only on the monthly lease payment, not the full vehicle price. On a $300K Ferrari, that's a savings of roughly $12,000–$15,000 compared to purchasing outright in a state that taxes the full amount.
  • Year-round driving weather: Unlike leasing a Ferrari in Chicago where it sits garaged five months a year, Miami's climate means you actually use the car. That makes the cost-per-smile ratio much more favorable.
  • Strong resale market: Miami's insatiable demand for Ferraris means residual values hold well, which translates to lower lease payments.

Where to Lease a Ferrari in Miami

The Collection — Coral Gables

The Collection at 200 Bird Road in Coral Gables is Miami's authorized Ferrari dealer and one of the top Ferrari retailers in the U.S. They handle the full Ferrari Financial Services lease process in-house. Expect white-glove service — literally. They'll deliver the car to your home or office if you prefer.

The Collection typically has 40–60 new Ferraris in stock, plus a strong selection of Certified Pre-Owned models eligible for CPO lease rates.

Third-Party Exotic Leasing

Companies like Premier Financial Services and Putnam Leasing offer alternative lease structures that can sometimes beat FFS terms, especially on pre-owned Ferraris. They're worth getting a quote from as a comparison.

Ferrari Lease Tips for Miami Buyers

1. Build a Relationship First

Ferrari operates on an allocation system. The most desirable models (SF90, 296 GTS Spider, and anything limited) go to clients with purchase history. If you're a first-time buyer, start with a Roma or Portofino M lease to establish yourself, then move up.

2. Watch Your Miles

Standard Ferrari leases come with 5,000–7,500 miles per year. In Miami, where everything is 20 minutes away and you'll want to cruise South Beach every weekend, that adds up fast. Negotiate for 10,000 miles/year upfront — it's much cheaper than paying overage fees at lease-end ($1–$2 per mile on a Ferrari).

3. Insurance Before You Sign

Get your insurance quote locked in before signing the lease. Ferrari insurance in Miami-Dade County runs $6,000–$15,000 annually depending on the model and your profile. The 296 GTB is particularly expensive to insure due to its hybrid powertrain complexity. Specialists like Hagerty, Chubb, and AIG Private Client often offer better rates than standard carriers.

4. Consider Certified Pre-Owned

Ferrari's CPO program ("Approved") covers vehicles up to 10 years old with a factory-backed warranty. Leasing a CPO Ferrari — say, a 2022 F8 Tributo with 5,000 miles — can save you $500–$1,000/month versus leasing new, with virtually the same driving experience.

Ferrari Lease vs. Buy: The Miami Calculus

In Miami's market, leasing a Ferrari makes financial sense for most buyers. Here's why:

  • Depreciation protection: You return the car at lease-end. If the market softens, that's Ferrari Financial's problem, not yours.
  • Variety: Miami's car scene moves fast. A 36-month lease means you're always in something current.
  • Tax efficiency: Business owners can often deduct a portion of lease payments. Consult your CPA, but the Section 179 and bonus depreciation angles are worth exploring.

The exception is limited-production models. If you can get allocated a Daytona SP3, F80, or other special series — buy it. Those appreciate, and you'll never get a lease deal that beats the equity upside.

Bottom Line on Ferrari Lease Deals in Miami

A Ferrari lease in Miami is more accessible than most people think. A Roma lease starts around $2,800/month with money down — roughly the cost of renting one for a single weekend. If you've been dreaming about it, start by visiting The Collection in Coral Gables, getting pre-qualified through Ferrari Financial Services, and budgeting for insurance. Miami is the best city in America to lease an exotic — the infrastructure, the culture, and the tax environment all work in your favor.

title: Best Ceramic Coating Kits for Cars: A Miami Exotic Owner's Guide
excerpt: Miami's sun, salt air, and constant UV exposure destroy paint faster than almost anywhere in the US. Here are the best ceramic coating kits to protect your exotic — from weekend warrior options to pro-grade systems.
content:
If you own an exotic car in Miami, ceramic coating isn't optional — it's survival. Between the relentless UV rays, salt-laden coastal air, afternoon thunderstorms, and the occasional bird that seems to target Ferraris specifically, your paint is under constant assault. A quality ceramic coating kit creates a semi-permanent shield that keeps your finish looking showroom-fresh for years.

We've tested and researched the top ceramic coating kits on the market in 2026, with a specific focus on what works best in South Florida's brutal conditions. Here's what's worth your money.

Why Ceramic Coating Matters More in Miami

Every car needs paint protection, but Miami's environment is uniquely hostile:

  • UV Index: Miami averages a UV index of 10+ for six months of the year. That's "extreme" on the scale. UV breaks down clear coat faster than almost any other factor.
  • Salt air: If you're within 10 miles of the coast (so… all of Miami), airborne salt is slowly corroding your paint, trim, and metal components 24/7.
  • Hard water: Miami's water is notoriously mineral-heavy. Every rain shower or car wash leaves water spots that can etch into unprotected clear coat.
  • Heat: Surface temperatures on a dark-colored exotic can exceed 170°F in a Miami parking lot. That heat accelerates chemical degradation of unprotected paint.

A ceramic coating with strong UV resistance, hydrophobic properties, and chemical bonding is your first line of defense.

Best Ceramic Coating Kits for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. Adam's Polishes UV Ceramic Paint Coating Kit — Best Overall

Price: ~$70 | Durability: 2–4 years | Difficulty: Intermediate

Adam's has become the go-to for enthusiasts who want pro-level results without the pro-level price tag. Their UV Ceramic Paint Coating Kit includes everything you need: the coating itself, prep spray, applicator pads, microfiber towels, and detailed instructions.

What makes it stand out for Miami use is the UV-resistant formula — it's specifically designed to handle intense sun exposure. The hydrophobic effect is excellent, meaning water beads and rolls off cleanly, taking contaminants with it.

Best for: Enthusiasts who want a balance of performance and ease of use.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. CarPro CQuartz UK 3.0 Kit — Best for Coastal Environments

Price: ~$75 | Durability: 2–3 years | Difficulty: Intermediate

CQuartz UK was originally formulated for the damp, harsh climate of the UK — and those same properties make it exceptional for Miami's salt air and humidity. The 3.0 version adds improved chemical resistance and a deeper gloss finish.

The kit includes CQuartz UK 3.0 coating, Eraser prep polish, and applicator suedes. You'll want to add your own microfiber towels. Application is straightforward if you've done any paint correction before.

Best for: Cars parked outdoors or near the coast. If your exotic lives in a Brickell high-rise garage but sees regular beach cruises, this is the one.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. Gtechniq Crystal Serum Light — Best Premium Option

Price: ~$90–110 | Durability: 3–5 years | Difficulty: Advanced

Gtechniq is what many professional detailers use on six- and seven-figure cars. Crystal Serum Light is the consumer version of their flagship Crystal Serum Ultra (which requires certified installer application). It offers 9H hardness — the highest scratch resistance rating available in a consumer coating.

The catch: application is less forgiving. You have a shorter working time before it flashes, and any mistakes are harder to correct. But if you're comfortable with the process, the results are stunning — deep, wet-look gloss with protection that lasts years.

Best for: Owners of high-value exotics (think $200K+) who want maximum protection and don't mind taking their time with application.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. Chemical Guys HydroSlick HyperWax Ceramic Coating — Best for Beginners

Price: ~$25–30 | Durability: 6–12 months | Difficulty: Easy

Let's be honest — not everyone wants to spend a full day doing paint correction and ceramic coating application. Chemical Guys HydroSlick is a ceramic-infused spray coating that goes on in minutes and provides genuine ceramic protection, just with shorter durability.

It's perfect as a maintenance layer between full ceramic coating applications, or as a standalone option for someone who wants to dip their toes into ceramic protection without the commitment.

Best for: First-timers, maintenance coats, or the "I have a McLaren but I'm not spending 8 hours in my garage" crowd.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. IGL Coatings Quartz+ — Best for Dark-Colored Exotics

Price: ~$80–100 | Durability: 3–5 years | Difficulty: Advanced

If you own a dark-colored exotic — Nero Daytona Ferrari, Nero Nemesis Lamborghini, Obsidian Black AMG — you know that swirl marks and micro-scratches are your worst enemy. IGL Quartz+ is formulated to fill those micro-imperfections while adding a layer of ceramic protection.

The result on dark paint is breathtaking: mirror-like depth that looks like the car is perpetually wet. It's a favorite among Miami's detailing shops for dark-colored customer cars.

Best for: Black, dark blue, dark green, or any deep-colored exotic that shows every imperfection.

→ Check price on Amazon

Ceramic Coating Comparison Table

ProductPriceDurabilityHardnessBest For
Adam's UV Ceramic Kit~$702–4 years9HOverall best value
CarPro CQuartz UK 3.0~$752–3 years9HCoastal/salt air protection
Gtechniq Crystal Serum Light~$90–1103–5 years9HHigh-value exotics
Chemical Guys HydroSlick~$25–306–12 monthsN/A (spray)Beginners & maintenance
IGL Quartz+~$80–1003–5 years9HDark-colored cars

How to Apply Ceramic Coating: Miami-Specific Tips

Timing Is Everything

Never apply ceramic coating in direct Miami sunlight. The ideal conditions are 65–80°F in a shaded garage with good ventilation. Early morning or evening in a climate-controlled garage is perfect. If you don't have a garage, consider renting bay time at a self-service detail shop — several in Hialeah and Doral rent by the hour.

Paint Correction First

Ceramic coating locks in whatever's underneath — including swirl marks, scratches, and oxidation. If your exotic has been daily-driven in Miami without protection, invest in a paint correction first. A dual-action polisher like the Griot's Garage G9 (~$150) paired with a cutting compound will remove years of damage.

Don't Forget the Trim and Wheels

Miami's road grime and brake dust are brutal on wheels. Apply ceramic coating to your wheels and calipers too — products like CarPro DLux are specifically designed for trim and wheels. Your future self will thank you every time brake dust wipes off with a rinse.

Professional vs. DIY in Miami

Professional ceramic coating application in Miami typically runs $800–$2,500 for an exotic car, depending on the product and the level of paint correction included. That's real money — but it's also guaranteed results with a warranty.

DIY kits at $70–$110 get you 80% of the way there at 5% of the cost. If you're comfortable with a polisher and have patience, the DIY route is absolutely viable for most enthusiasts.

Our recommendation: Do it yourself for daily drivers and "attainable" exotics. Spring for professional installation on anything worth $300K+ or with irreplaceable factory paint (looking at you, Porsche PTS colors).

Bottom Line

In Miami, ceramic coating isn't vanity — it's maintenance. The Adam's UV Ceramic Kit is our top pick for most exotic owners, offering the best balance of protection, ease of use, and value. For maximum longevity on high-dollar paint, step up to Gtechniq Crystal Serum Light. And if you just want quick protection with minimal effort, Chemical Guys HydroSlick gets the job done in minutes.

Your Miami exotic deserves better than bare clear coat. Coat it. 🛡️

title: Best Dash Cams for Exotic Cars: Protect Your Miami Investment
excerpt: Between Miami's aggressive drivers, parking lot door dings, and insurance fraud attempts, a high-end dash cam is essential gear for any exotic car owner. Here are the best options for 2026.
content:
You just parked your $250K Lamborghini at Aventura Mall. You come back to find a fresh scratch on the quarter panel and zero witnesses. Or you're cruising down I-95 when someone brake-checks you in an obvious insurance scam. Or your Ferrari gets keyed overnight in your Brickell parking garage.

All of these happen regularly in Miami. And all of them are solvable with one piece of equipment: a high-quality dash cam.

For exotic car owners, a dash cam isn't just a convenience — it's insurance for your insurance. We've evaluated the top dash cams for exotic cars based on video quality, parking mode capabilities, heat resistance (critical in Miami), and discreet installation options.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need a Dash Cam

Miami-Dade County has some of the highest rates of auto insurance fraud, hit-and-runs, and uninsured drivers in the United States. Combine that with the fact that you're driving a vehicle worth more than most people's houses, and the math is simple:

  • Insurance fraud: Miami is the #1 city in the US for staged accidents. A dash cam is your best defense against false claims.
  • Hit and runs: Florida ranks #1 nationally for hit-and-run fatalities. If someone clips your exotic and bolts, you need footage.
  • Parking incidents: Between valet damage, garage door dings, and vandalism, parking mode recording is essential.
  • Insurance discounts: Some high-value vehicle insurers (Hagerty, Chubb) offer premium discounts for vehicles equipped with dash cams.

Best Dash Cams for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. BlackVue DR970X-2CH Plus — Best Overall for Exotics

Price: ~$400–450 | Resolution: 4K Front + 1080p Rear | Parking Mode: Yes (hardwired)

The BlackVue DR970X is the gold standard for exotic car dash cams, and for good reason. The front camera shoots in true 4K with Sony STARVIS 2 sensor technology, capturing license plates clearly even at highway speeds. The rear camera records in Full HD.

What sets BlackVue apart for Miami use:

  • Cloud connectivity: Built-in WiFi and optional LTE. You can check your car's live feed from your phone while you're at dinner. If someone hits your parked car, you get an instant push notification with footage.
  • Parking mode: With a hardwire kit or the BlackVue battery pack, the camera records continuously while parked — detecting motion and impacts. This alone justifies the price for any exotic owner.
  • Heat resistance: Rated for operation up to 158°F (70°C). Critical when your dash hits 160°F+ under Miami summer sun.

Best for: The owner who wants comprehensive, always-on protection with remote monitoring.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Thinkware U3000 2-Channel — Best Video Quality

Price: ~$450–500 | Resolution: 4K Front + 2K Rear | Parking Mode: Yes (hardwired)

Thinkware's flagship U3000 pushes video quality even further with a 4K front camera and a 2K (QHD) rear camera — currently the highest combined resolution available. The image processing is outstanding, with excellent night vision thanks to their Super Night Vision 4.0 technology.

The U3000 also features radar-based parking surveillance, which is more power-efficient than motion detection alone. It can distinguish between a passing pedestrian (no alert) and someone approaching your car (alert + recording). Smart and efficient.

Best for: Owners who prioritize the absolute best video evidence quality, especially for nighttime recording.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. BlackVue DR770X-2CH LTE Plus — Best Connected Option

Price: ~$370–400 | Resolution: 1080p Front + 1080p Rear | Parking Mode: Yes

If built-in LTE connectivity is your priority — and for Miami exotic owners, it should be high on the list — the DR770X LTE Plus is the sweet spot. It has a built-in SIM slot for always-on cellular connectivity, meaning you can stream live footage, receive impact alerts, and check GPS location from anywhere.

Video quality is 1080p (not 4K), which is a step down from the DR970X, but still more than adequate for license plate capture and insurance documentation. The LTE connectivity makes up for it with real-time peace of mind.

Best for: Owners who want real-time monitoring and GPS tracking. Excellent if you valet your car frequently (and you know you do in Miami).

→ Check price on Amazon

4. Garmin Dash Cam 67W — Best Compact/Discreet Option

Price: ~$230–260 | Resolution: 1440p Front | Parking Mode: Yes (with cable)

Some exotic owners don't want a visible dash cam disrupting their interior aesthetic. The Garmin 67W is one of the smallest, most discreet dash cams available — about the size of a car key fob. It tucks behind the rearview mirror and is virtually invisible from outside the car.

Despite its size, it records in 1440p with a 180-degree field of view (the widest in its class), includes voice control, and connects to the Garmin Drive app for footage review. Parking mode is available with the optional constant power cable.

Best for: Owners who want protection without visible equipment. Great for cars with minimalist interiors (McLaren, Porsche) where a bulky cam would look out of place.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. VIOFO A229 Pro 3CH — Best Three-Channel System

Price: ~$300–350 | Resolution: 4K Front + 2K Interior + 2K Rear | Parking Mode: Yes

For exotic owners who want maximum coverage — front, interior, and rear — the VIOFO A229 Pro delivers three cameras in one system. The interior camera is particularly useful if you lend your car to friends, use valet services, or want to document what happens inside the cabin during a service appointment.

At roughly $300, it's also the best value three-channel system on the market. Video quality is excellent across all three cameras, with Sony STARVIS 2 sensors throughout.

Best for: Owners who use valet frequently, lend their car, or want interior documentation. Also excellent as a theft deterrent.

→ Check price on Amazon

Dash Cam Comparison Table

Dash CamPriceFront ResolutionRear/InteriorParking ModeCloud/LTE
BlackVue DR970X-2CH Plus~$400–4504K1080p rear✅WiFi + optional LTE
Thinkware U3000 2CH~$450–5004K2K rear✅ (radar)WiFi + optional LTE
BlackVue DR770X LTE Plus~$370–4001080p1080p rear✅Built-in LTE
Garmin 67W~$230–2601440pFront only✅ (cable req.)WiFi only
VIOFO A229 Pro 3CH~$300–3504K2K int. + 2K rear✅WiFi only

Installation Tips for Exotic Cars

Hardwiring Is Non-Negotiable

For parking mode to work, you need constant power. A BlackVue Power Magic Ultra battery pack (~$230) is the cleanest solution — it powers the dash cam while parked without tapping your car's battery. For exotics with sensitive electrical systems (looking at you, Ferrari and McLaren), an external battery pack is safer than hardwiring to the fuse box.

Professional Installation Recommended

On a $300K+ car, don't DIY the wiring. Miami has several shops that specialize in dash cam installation on exotics:

  • Prestige Auto Sound on Biscayne Blvd — experienced with Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and McLarens
  • Most authorized dealership service departments will install or refer you to a trusted installer

Professional installation typically runs $150–$300 and ensures clean cable routing with zero visible wires.

Miami Heat Considerations

This is critical: standard dash cams with capacitor-based power (not lithium batteries) handle Miami heat far better. All five cameras recommended above use supercapacitors instead of lithium batteries. Cheap dash cams with lithium batteries can swell, malfunction, or even catch fire in Miami's extreme heat. Don't risk it on your exotic.

Do Dash Cams Lower Insurance Premiums?

Potentially, yes. While most standard insurers don't offer explicit dash cam discounts, specialty exotic car insurers are increasingly considering them:

  • Hagerty: May reduce premiums for vehicles with documented security/monitoring systems
  • Chubb Private Client: Has been known to factor dash cams into risk assessment
  • Pure Insurance: Offers discounts for comprehensive vehicle monitoring

Even without a direct discount, having dash cam footage can dramatically speed up claims processing and prevent fraudulent claims — which keeps your rates from skyrocketing after an incident that wasn't your fault.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the BlackVue DR970X-2CH Plus is the move. It offers the best combination of video quality, parking mode, cloud connectivity, and heat resilience. If budget is a concern, the VIOFO A229 Pro 3CH delivers outstanding value with three-channel coverage.

A $400 dash cam protecting a $300,000 car is the best ROI in automotive accessories. In Miami, it's not if you'll need the footage — it's when. 📹

title: Rolls-Royce Phantom for Sale in Miami: Where to Look in 2026
excerpt: The Rolls-Royce Phantom is the ultimate luxury sedan, and Miami is one of the best cities in the world to buy one. Here is your complete guide to finding a Rolls-Royce Phantom for sale in Miami.
content:
The Rolls-Royce Phantom is the pinnacle of automotive luxury. No other car combines presence, craftsmanship, and sheer opulence quite like the Phantom — and no city suits it better than Miami. Whether you're cruising down Collins Avenue, pulling up to LIV, or simply making a silent statement in the valet line at Zuma, the Phantom is the undisputed king.

If you're searching for a Rolls-Royce Phantom for sale in Miami, you're in the right market. South Florida has one of the highest concentrations of Rolls-Royce inventory in the United States. Here's everything you need to know.

Rolls-Royce Phantom for Sale: 2026 Pricing in Miami

The Phantom is Rolls-Royce's flagship sedan, and pricing reflects its position at the absolute top of the luxury market:

ModelYear RangeApprox. Price (Miami)Key Features
Phantom VIII (new)2024–2026$460,000 – $650,000+Current gen, bespoke gallery, 6.75L V12
Phantom VIII (pre-owned)2018–2023$275,000 – $420,000Same generation, significant savings
Phantom Extended2018–2026$500,000 – $700,000+Long wheelbase, rear-seat luxury focus
Phantom VII (previous gen)2012–2017$120,000 – $220,000Classic design, V12, excellent value
Phantom Drophead Coupe2007–2016$180,000 – $350,000Convertible, highly collectible

The sweet spot for most Miami buyers is a pre-owned Phantom VIII from 2019–2022 with under 20,000 miles. These cars have taken their biggest depreciation hit and can be found for $280,000–$350,000 — roughly half of the original sticker price — while still looking and driving like new.

Where to Buy a Rolls-Royce Phantom in Miami

Braman Rolls-Royce — The Authorized Dealer

Braman Motors in West Palm Beach (with strong ties to the Miami market) is South Florida's authorized Rolls-Royce dealer. They're the only place to buy a new Phantom with full factory warranty and access to the Bespoke program, which lets you customize virtually every element of your car.

Braman typically stocks 3–6 new Phantoms and a rotating selection of Rolls-Royce Certified Pre-Owned models. Their CPO program includes a comprehensive inspection and extended warranty — meaningful peace of mind on a car with a $15,000+ annual maintenance budget.

Why buy here: Factory warranty, Bespoke ordering, Certified Pre-Owned program, and a dedicated Rolls-Royce service center.

Prestige Imports — Pre-Owned Luxury

While primarily known as Miami's Lamborghini dealer, Prestige Imports on Biscayne Boulevard regularly stocks pre-owned Rolls-Royces, including Phantoms. They often have competitive pricing compared to the franchise dealer and are conveniently located in North Miami Beach.

Curated — Gallery-Style Selection

Curated in Wynwood occasionally features exceptional Phantom specs — think low-mileage, rare Bespoke colors, or historically significant examples. If you want a Phantom that's a conversation piece beyond just being a Phantom, check their inventory.

Independent Dealers & Private Sales

Miami's independent exotic dealer network — including RMC Miami, iLusso, and Exotic Car Trader — frequently list pre-owned Phantoms at 5–15% below franchise dealer pricing. The trade-off is no factory CPO warranty, so a thorough pre-purchase inspection by a Rolls-Royce specialist is essential.

Private sales through platforms like Bring a Trailer, Cars & Bids, and DuPont Registry can also yield excellent deals on Phantoms, particularly Generation VII models.

Rolls-Royce Phantom: What Makes It Special

For buyers new to the Phantom, here's what separates it from every other luxury sedan on the market:

The Engine

A 6.75-liter twin-turbocharged V12 producing 563 horsepower and 664 lb-ft of torque. But the numbers don't tell the story — the Phantom's V12 delivers its power with a supernatural smoothness that Rolls-Royce calls "waftability." You don't feel acceleration; you feel the world receding behind you.

The Cabin

The Phantom's interior uses more leather than a furniture showroom. Every surface is hand-stitched, hand-polished, or hand-finished. The Starlight Headliner — fiber optic lights embedded in the roof that replicate a night sky — is the signature feature, and it never gets old. The Generation VIII added the Gallery dashboard, a glass-enclosed display area that owners can commission with artwork, embroidery, or precious metals.

The Ride

Rolls-Royce's "Magic Carpet Ride" air suspension uses cameras to read the road ahead and pre-adjust the dampers. On Miami's pothole-laden roads — we're looking at you, Brickell — this is genuinely transformative. The Phantom floats where other luxury sedans merely absorb.

Cost of Ownership in Miami

Owning a Phantom in Miami is a commitment beyond the purchase price:

  • Insurance: $6,000–$14,000/year in Miami-Dade County, depending on your profile and coverage. Specialty insurers like Chubb and AIG Private Client typically offer the best rates for ultra-luxury vehicles.
  • Maintenance: Annual service at Braman runs $3,000–$5,000 for routine maintenance. Major services (every 4 years) can reach $8,000–12,000. Tires alone cost $1,500–$2,500 for a set, and the Phantom chews through rears faster than you'd expect.
  • Depreciation: A new Phantom loses roughly 30–40% in the first three years. This is why buying a 2–3 year old example is often the smartest play — let someone else absorb the steepest depreciation.
  • Fuel: The V12 returns roughly 12–14 MPG in Miami driving. Budget accordingly.

Phantom vs. Ghost vs. Spectre: Which Rolls-Royce for Miami?

Rolls-Royce now offers three sedans, and each suits a different Miami buyer:

ModelStarting PriceCharacterBest For
Phantom~$460,000Ultimate luxury, rear-seat focusedBeing chauffeured, maximum presence
Ghost~$340,000Driver's luxury sedan, more agileOwners who drive themselves daily
Spectre~$420,000Electric ultra-luxury coupeTech-forward, silent cruising

The Phantom is the choice if presence and rear-seat luxury are paramount — if you're regularly driven by a chauffeur, entertaining clients, or simply want the biggest, most commanding Rolls-Royce available. The Ghost is better if you prefer to drive yourself and want something slightly more manageable in Miami traffic.

Tips for Buying a Rolls-Royce Phantom in Miami

  1. Inspect the Starlight Headliner: On pre-owned models, check that all fiber optic strands are functioning. Repairs are expensive — $5,000+ to replace a section.
  2. Check the air suspension: Listen for compressor noise and check for uneven ride height. Air strut replacement runs $3,000–5,000 per corner.
  3. Verify Bespoke features: Many Phantoms have one-of-a-kind specifications. Verify all custom elements are documented, as they significantly affect resale value.
  4. Salt air protection: Miami's coastal environment is hard on chrome and brightwork. Inspect for any pitting or corrosion on trim pieces, especially on cars that have been parked outdoors.
  5. Get a PPI: Always. Even on a CPO car. A Rolls-Royce specialist PPI costs $500–$800 and can save you tens of thousands in hidden issues.

Bottom Line

If you're looking for a Rolls-Royce Phantom for sale in Miami, the market in 2026 is favorable for buyers. Pre-owned inventory is healthy, prices have normalized from the pandemic-era frenzy, and South Florida's dealer network gives you plenty of options to find the right spec. Start at Braman for new and CPO models, check Curated and Prestige for unique pre-owned examples, and don't overlook the VII generation if you want Phantom presence at a more accessible price point.

The Rolls-Royce Phantom isn't just a car — it's a declaration. And in Miami, declarations are always welcome.

title: Leasing an Aston Martin in Miami: Complete 2026 Guide
excerpt: An Aston Martin lease in Miami is more attainable than you think. Here is your complete guide to Aston Martin lease deals, monthly payments, the best models to lease, and where to go in South Florida.
content:
There's something about an Aston Martin that hits different in Miami. While Ferraris and Lamborghinis scream for attention, an Aston Martin whispers — and everyone leans in to listen. It's the choice of the driver who has nothing to prove, and in Miami's often-flashy car scene, that restraint is its own kind of statement.

If you've been considering an Aston Martin lease, Miami is one of the best cities in America to do it. Between Florida's tax advantages, year-round driving weather, and a strong local dealer network, leasing an Aston Martin here makes more financial sense than almost anywhere else. Here's how it works in 2026.

Aston Martin Lease Deals: 2026 Monthly Payments

Aston Martin Financial Services (AMFS) handles leasing through authorized dealers. Lease terms and payments vary by model, but here's what Miami buyers can expect:

ModelMSRP RangeTypical Lease (36 mo.)Down PaymentResidual Value
Vantage (2025+)$165,000 – $195,000$1,800 – $2,400/mo$15,000 – $25,00052–58%
DB12$245,000 – $290,000$2,800 – $3,500/mo$25,000 – $40,00050–55%
DBX707$235,000 – $280,000$2,600 – $3,200/mo$25,000 – $35,00048–53%
Vanquish (2025+)$320,000 – $380,000$3,800 – $4,600/mo$35,000 – $50,00048–52%

These estimates assume strong credit (700+), first-time Aston Martin buyer status, and Miami-area dealer pricing. Existing Aston Martin clients with purchase history can often negotiate better money factors — sometimes significantly so.

Why Lease an Aston Martin in Miami?

Leasing makes particular sense for Aston Martins, and Miami amplifies the advantages:

Florida Tax Benefits

  • No state income tax: More disposable income for that monthly payment.
  • Sales tax on lease payments only: In Florida, you pay sales tax on the monthly payment, not the full vehicle price. On a $250K DB12, this saves you $10,000–12,000 compared to states that tax the full amount at purchase.

Depreciation Protection

Aston Martins historically depreciate faster than their Italian and German competitors. A new DB12 can lose 35–45% of its value in three years. Leasing shifts that depreciation risk to the finance company. When the lease ends, you hand back the keys and move on — or into the next model.

Always Drive Current

Aston Martin is in the middle of a product renaissance. The new Vantage, DB12, and upcoming Vanquish represent a generational leap in performance and technology. A 36-month lease keeps you in the latest model without the long-term commitment.

Year-Round Enjoyment

Unlike leasing an Aston in Boston or Chicago, where it sits garaged half the year, Miami's climate means you're driving it 365 days. Your cost per drive drops dramatically.

Where to Lease an Aston Martin in Miami

Aston Martin Miami — The Authorized Dealer

Aston Martin Miami (formerly The Collection's Aston Martin division) is the city's authorized dealer, located at 200 Bird Road in Coral Gables alongside The Collection's Ferrari, Maserati, and Alfa Romeo showrooms. They handle Aston Martin Financial Services leasing directly and typically stock 20–35 new and pre-owned Aston Martins.

Why go here: Factory-backed lease rates, access to limited allocations, Aston Martin Timeless (CPO) program, and a service center with factory-trained technicians. They also offer track day experiences at Homestead-Miami Speedway for new clients — a serious perk.

Third-Party Exotic Leasing

Companies like Premier Financial Services and Putnam Leasing specialize in exotic car leases and can sometimes offer more flexible terms than the factory program — especially on pre-owned Aston Martins. They're worth getting a competitive quote from, particularly if you're leasing a pre-owned model that isn't eligible for AMFS rates.

Best Aston Martin Models to Lease in Miami

Vantage — Best Value Lease

The 2025+ Vantage is the entry point to Aston Martin ownership, but calling it "entry-level" undersells it completely. The Mercedes-AMG-sourced 4.0L twin-turbo V8 now produces 656 horsepower — making it the most powerful Vantage ever. It's compact, aggressive, and sounds phenomenal with the exhaust in Sport+ mode echoing off Brickell's towers.

At under $2,000/month with money down, it's the most accessible Aston Martin lease and arguably the best-looking sports car in its price range.

DB12 — Best All-Rounder

The DB12 replaced the DB11 and earned the title of the world's first "Super Tourer." It's the car you take on a weekend drive to Naples, park at the valet at Nobu, and still enjoy on a Tuesday commute. With 671 horsepower from the twin-turbo V8, gorgeous proportions, and a cabin that rivals anything from Bentley, the DB12 is the quintessential Miami grand tourer.

For convertible lovers, the DB12 Volante is the ultimate Miami Aston — top down, crossing the Rickenbacker Causeway at sunset. If you're going to lease one car that defines the Miami lifestyle, this might be it.

DBX707 — Best Daily Driver

The DBX707 is the world's most powerful luxury SUV — 707 horsepower in a vehicle that can handle school runs, airport pickups, and weekend getaways. It's Aston Martin's answer to the Lamborghini Urus, with more refinement and (arguably) better looks.

For Miami buyers who need practicality but refuse to sacrifice performance or style, the DBX707 lease is compelling. It handles Miami's speed bumps and parking garages without drama while still turning heads at every stoplight.

Aston Martin Lease Tips for Miami Buyers

1. Negotiate the Money Factor

The money factor (essentially the interest rate) on an Aston Martin lease is negotiable, especially if you have strong credit and are willing to put more money down. Even a small reduction in money factor can save $100–200/month on a $250K vehicle.

2. Watch Your Miles

Standard Aston Martin leases include 7,500–10,000 miles per year. Miami's compact geography helps here — most destinations are within 20 miles. But if you plan weekend trips to Key West, Naples, or Orlando, negotiate for 12,000 miles/year upfront. Overage fees are typically $0.50–$1.00 per mile.

3. Get Insurance Quotes First

Aston Martin insurance in Miami-Dade County runs $4,000–$10,000 annually depending on the model and your profile. The DBX707 is surprisingly affordable to insure compared to the sports cars. Get quotes from Hagerty, Chubb, and AIG Private Client before signing — they consistently beat standard carriers for exotic vehicles.

4. Consider Aston Martin Timeless (CPO)

Aston Martin's certified pre-owned program, called "Timeless," covers cars up to 10 years old with a factory-backed warranty. Leasing a Timeless DB11 or previous-gen Vantage can save $500–800/month versus leasing new, with minimal compromise on the driving experience.

5. Explore Business Lease Options

If you're a business owner — and this is Miami, so statistically you might be — consult your CPA about deducting lease payments. The Section 179 deduction and bonus depreciation rules can make a meaningful dent in the effective cost of a DBX707 lease in particular, given its weight qualifies for enhanced deductions.

Aston Martin Lease vs. Buy: The Math

For most Aston Martin models, leasing wins the financial argument:

  • Depreciation: Aston Martins lose 35–45% in three years. On a $250K DB12, that's $87,000–$112,000 in depreciation. A lease caps your exposure.
  • Warranty alignment: The factory warranty covers the full lease term, so you're never out of pocket for surprise repairs.
  • Model freshness: With Aston Martin releasing significant updates every 2–3 years, leasing keeps you current.

The exception: if Aston Martin releases a limited-production model and you get an allocation (like the Valour or upcoming Valhalla), buying makes more sense — limited models tend to hold value or appreciate.

Aston Martin in Miami: More Than a Car

Aston Martin Miami doesn't just sell cars — they offer a lifestyle ecosystem. Owners get access to:

  • Art of Living experiences: Private events, motorsport experiences, and curated lifestyle events throughout South Florida
  • Aston Martin Residences: Miami's 66-story Aston Martin-branded luxury tower in Downtown, with a unique tie-in for car owners
  • Track events: Regular track days at Homestead-Miami Speedway exclusively for Aston Martin owners

The Aston Martin Residences at 300 Biscayne Boulevard Way are particularly noteworthy — it's one of the few places where you can live in your car brand. Penthouse buyers even receive an Aston Martin Vulcan as part of the purchase. The building's car elevator and private garage suites are designed specifically for Aston Martin ownership.

Bottom Line on Aston Martin Leasing in Miami

An Aston Martin lease in Miami starts at roughly $1,800/month for a Vantage — less than renting one for a single weekend. With Florida's tax advantages, year-round driving weather, and one of the best authorized dealer experiences in the country, Miami is arguably the best city in America to lease an Aston Martin.

Start at Aston Martin Miami in Coral Gables, test drive the DB12 Volante across the causeway, and see if you can hand back the keys. We bet you can't.
